summary.headline: The Conservation Commission continued hearings on a Lynbrook Road water main relining and a contentious 0 Southville Road apartment proposal.
summary.summary: The Southborough Conservation Commission reviewed a town DPW proposal to rehabilitate water mains along Lynbrook Road using cured-in-place pipe lining, continuing the hearing to allow plan revisions. The commission also opened a hearing for a proposed multi-family development at 0 Southville Road under the MBTA Communities zoning overlay, which drew significant pushback from neighbors regarding environmental protection, fire safety, and previous site violations. In other business, commissioners approved a Certificate of Compliance for 26 Meadow Lane, discussed new enforcement regulations for conservation land, and received updates on regional clean energy permitting rules and commercial redevelopments.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The commission handled procedural tasks, including approving past meeting minutes and adjourning at the conclusion of business.
key_details: Approved minutes of January 29, 2026.
The meeting adjourned at approximately 8:32 PM.
topics.outcome: Minutes approved 5-0-1 with one abstention; meeting adjourned.

topics.title: Lynbrook Road water main rehabilitation NOI
topics.summary: The Department of Public Works submitted a Notice of Intent to rehabilitate an aging water main running from Main Street through an easement along Interstate 495 to Lynbrook Road and Lovers Lane. Rather than open trench excavation through wetland areas, the project will use a cured-in-place pipe structural lining within the existing 12-inch asbestos-cement pipe.
key_details: Project limits stretch between Route 30 (Main Street) and Lovers Lane along Lynbrook Road.
Work in the buffer zone is limited to 280 square feet of excavation across temporary access pits spaced roughly 400 feet apart.
Lynbrook Road is technically a state highway, and the town is coordinating the project ahead of MassDOT repaving and transferring the road to the town.
The commission consultant requested clarifying details on dewatering protocols, erosion barriers, and perennial stream distances.
The hearing was continued to allow the applicant to provide revised plans and construction details.
topics.outcome: Hearing continued to April 2, 2026 at 7:00 PM.

topics.title: 0 Southville Road apartment development NOI and Stormwater Permit
topics.summary: Applicant Apartments at Southville Road LLC presented an initial Notice of Intent and Stormwater Management Permit application to construct two apartment buildings and a clubhouse on a 4-acre parcel at 0 Southville Road (Map 5, Lot 8) in the MBTA Communities Overlay District. The applicant and commissioners agreed the review is at an early stage because snow cover prevented on-site wetland confirmation, an existing 2021 wetland delineation order expires in April, and past unauthorized tree clearing on the property needs to be reviewed.
key_details: Proposed project includes two apartment buildings and a clubhouse on approximately 4 acres.
The site has an existing Order of Resource Area Delineation from 2021 that remains valid until April 23, 2026.
Commissioners noted an earlier enforcement order regarding unpermitted clearing in the riverfront and buffer zone must be reviewed to establish the lawful baseline for development.
Neighbors raised concerns regarding zoning compliance under the MBTA overlay, fire apparatus access, snow and trash storage, and potential impacts on Sudbury River aquatic habitats.
The applicant requested an extended continuance to allow snow to melt, walk the site with town consultants, and revise the design.
topics.why_it_matters: The proposal introduces high-density multi-family housing near the Sudbury River under the town's MBTA zoning overlay, prompting scrutiny over wetland protections, site safety, and allowable uses.

topics.title: 26 Meadow Lane Certificate of Compliance
topics.summary: The commission reviewed a Request for Certificate of Compliance for DEP File 290-1087 at 26 Meadow Lane, involving a trench drain installed several years ago to manage high groundwater near the Carriage Hill septic system. The conservation agent confirmed that the required two years of invasive species monitoring reports had been submitted with positive results.
key_details: Applies to DEP File 290-1087 at 26 Meadow Lane.
Work involved a trench drain to address groundwater around septic infrastructure.
Two years of invasive species management and monitoring reports were completed.

topics.title: Conservation land use regulations
topics.summary: The conservation agent presented a draft set of formal land use regulations governing town-owned conservation parcels under the Conservation Commission Act. The regulations establish explicit rules and enforceable penalties for encroachment, dumping, unauthorized trail cutting, and open fires, with distinct provisions tailored for Breakneck Hill.
key_details: Creates two sets of rules: one specific to Breakneck Hill and one general set for all other town conservation properties.
Rules establish property hours from dawn to dusk, restrict unauthorized trail building, prohibit hunting and dumping, and ban open fires except by special permit.
Establishes a fine and ticketing mechanism that police and town staff can enforce against property encroachment or vandalism.
The Breakneck Hill Stewardship Committee will review the draft regulations at its March 19 meeting.
A formal public hearing will be scheduled before the regulations are adopted and filed with the town clerk.
topics.outcome: Discussion held; draft language will be refined regarding fire permissions and reviewed by committees prior to a formal public hearing.

topics.title: Conservation agent project updates and state clean energy rules
topics.summary: The conservation agent briefed the commission on several ongoing projects and state regulatory developments. Topics included revised 40B filings for 250 Turnpike Road, on-site demolition preparation at 21 Coslin Street for a planned Costco redevelopment, and new Department of Energy Resources regulations taking effect in October that mandate a 12-month consolidated local permitting process for small clean energy projects.
key_details: 250 Turnpike Road (Beehive) submitted revised comprehensive permit materials to the Zoning Board of Appeals.
Demolition of existing structures at 21 Coslin Street is starting under Westborough and Southborough oversight ahead of Costco site plan filings.
DOER regulations taking effect in October require towns to process small clean energy applications (solar, battery storage) under a single consolidated local permit within 12 months.
If a town board denies a clean energy project or misses deadlines, the applicant can appeal directly to the state Energy Facilities Siting Board.
topics.outcome: Informational updates accepted; no formal votes taken.

votes.motion: Continue the public hearing for the Lynbrook Road water main replacement Notice of Intent to April 2, 2026 at 7:00 PM.
Continue the public hearing for 0 Southville Road Notice of Intent and Stormwater Management Permit to April 30, 2026.
Issue a Certificate of Compliance for DEP File 290-1087 at 26 Meadow Lane.

public_comment.summary: A resident of Southville Road raised several concerns on behalf of neighbors regarding the proposed 0 Southville Road development, pointing out that the MBTA overlay district does not allow variances, questioning the permissibility of a detached clubhouse and front parking, expressing worry about fire safety along the railroad tracks, noting a lack of designated snow and trash storage, and emphasizing the ecological sensitivity of the Sudbury River corridor and BioMap core habitat.

The DPW superintendent commented as an attendee, stating that the project presentation for 0 Southville Road lacked adequate substance and detail for abutters who attended to learn about the development scope.

A Southville Road resident clarified that neighbors had attended previous planning sessions, reviewed the submitted plans closely, and intend to remain engaged throughout the conservation and planning board review processes.

Breakneck Hill Stewardship Committee meeting to review draft conservation land regulations
Continued public hearing on 0 Southville Road apartment development Notice of Intent and Stormwater Permit
